subject: Ledger audit clearance — confirmation no customer records accessed
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha@finnova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: LedgerWorks Security <security@ledgerworks.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident question — ledger store exposure?

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the update earlier in the status page. Our security team asked us to confirm whether any of our customer ledger rows or unique identifiers were read or exported during the incident window (2027-04-18 02:00 UTC — 2027-04-18 04:30 UTC). FinnovA handles regulated account identifiers and we need a short statement for our internal compliance review.

Can you confirm whether there was any read access to our ledger objects, and if there were any outbound transfers or S3 PUT/GETs that match our account prefixes? If you can point us to the specific logs or checks you ran, that would be great.

We appreciate the quick turnaround — even a short "no records accessed" confirmation will help us close the ticket.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Senior Security Ops, FinnovA

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@finnova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident question — ledger store exposure?

Hi Aisha —

Short answer: at this stage our forensic checks show no reads of FinnovA ledger records and no outbound transfers tied to your account prefixes.

What we ran so far (summary):
- Access log reconciliation: scanned API logs and object-storage access events for prefixes finnova/ledger/* and finnova/meta/*. No GET/HEAD/OBJECT_COPY events during the incident window. (see attachment: access-log-sample.txt)
- Hash reconciliation: compared daily ledger digest snapshots against post-incident snapshots; no unexplained delta for keys owned by FinnovA.
- Ephemeral cache sweep: validated KV-cache invalidations completed; no long-lived cached payloads matched FinnovA patterns.

Attachments included: ledger-audit-summary.csv (summary of hashes and counts) and access-log-sample.txt (excerpts). These are preliminary; Marcus and Connor are doing a deeper run (full-object-check + signed checksum).

If you need a notarized checksum or signed artifact for audits I can escalate to Naomi for a formal statement. Expect a fuller response by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aisha Malik <aisha@finnova.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 18:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident question — ledger store exposure?

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 11:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Aisha —
> 
> Short answer: at this stage our forensic checks show no reads of FinnovA ledger records and no outbound transfers tied to your account prefixes.
> 
> What we ran so far (summary):
> - Access log reconciliation...

Adding the technical detail from the deeper verification run: we executed an object-level reconcile across the snapshot sets for 2027-04-17 and 2027-04-19 with the following checks:

1) Signed checksum verification: re-hashed each ledger blob (SHA256) and compared against immutable daily digests; all FinnovA objects matched expected checksums. No new objects discovered with matching FinnovA prefix that lacked a prior digest.
2) Storage access pattern scan: queried audit trail for S3 GET/HEAD/ACL events originating from ephemeral worker IP ranges that were implicated in the incident. No events referencing finnova/ledger/* were found between 2027-04-18T02:00Z and 2027-04-18T05:00Z (we expanded window by 30 minutes to be conservative).
3) Outbound egress trace: scanned egress proxies and S3 transfer logs for PUT or COPY to external buckets. There were two automated backups performed outside the window; neither referenced FinnovA prefixes.

Representative log excerpt (redacted):
2027-04-18T02:14:23Z GET s3://redwood-prod/fin.../ledger/sha256:ab12... user=svc-ingest ip=10.4.8.23 result=403
2027-04-18T02:16:05Z PUT s3://redwood-backups/auto/2027-04-17 ... user=svc-backup result=200

Conclusion: technical evidence shows no read or exfiltration of FinnovA ledger objects. We're preparing a signed checksum bundle plus chain-of-custody notes.

-Marcus
Senior Forensics Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@finnova.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: LedgerWorks Security <security@ledgerworks.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Formal confirmation: FinnovA ledger audit & non-exposure statement

Aisha —

Following the technical reconciliation that Marcus summarized, this is Redwood's formal written confirmation for your compliance record: 

- Scope: objects with prefix finnova/ledger/* and associated metadata for the incident window 2027-04-18T02:00:00Z through 2027-04-18T04:30:00Z (expanded window to 2027-04-18T05:00:00Z for conservative coverage).
- Findings: No successful read (GET/HEAD/OBJECT_COPY) or unauthorized transfer was observed for objects matching FinnovA prefixes in the expanded window. Daily immutable digests and object-level SHA256 rehashes are consistent; no missing or altered blobs were detected.
- Evidence artifacts: attached signed checksum bundle (checksum-report-signed.pdf), supporting CSV digest summary (ledger-audit-summary.csv), and a short list of sampled access entries (access-log-sample.txt). For convenience we included presigned links to full artifacts in s3-presigned-links.txt (valid 7 days).
- Chain of custody: all verification steps were logged; the checksum bundle includes timestamps and the verifier identity and has been retained in our compliance archive.

If you require a notarized affidavit or an on-call walk-through with your audit team, please let me know and we will schedule it. We are committed to supporting your regulator submission.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Forwarded attachments: checksum-report-signed.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), ledger-audit-summary.csv (CSV), access-log-sample.txt (TXT), s3-presigned-links.txt (TXT)
